strengths: Novel discovery of hallucinated minimizers as a previously unrecognized failure mode of SAM, distinct from saddle points and surrogate-based issues

Rigorous theoretical analysis with elegant proofs: existence theorems (2.1, 2.2) using Lagrange multipliers and Łojasiewicz inequality, geometric structure preservation (Theorem 3.1), and convergence dynamics (Theorem 3.2)
Comprehensive characterization revealing that hallucinated minimizers arise near high-loss regions with local maximizers and form attractors of SAM dynamics
Clear, well-presented exposition with excellent intuition and visualization, particularly the geometric illustration of the proof method
Practical and effective solution: simple switching strategy (GD→SAM) that stabilizes training across perturbation radii and improves test accuracy consistently
Good empirical validation spanning synthetic 2D examples, full-batch MNIST experiments, and realistic CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18
Systematic experimental analysis showing how hallucinated minimizer convergence depends on perturbation radius ρ
Strong reproducibility with complete proofs, detailed appendices, experimental details, and code availability
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap on activation functions: theoretical results require real-analyticity but exclude ReLU (ubiquitous in practice), while experiments use ReLU networks not covered by theory

Loose connection between theoretical conditions and empirical phenomena: Theorems assume isolated/bounded maximizer sets whose presence in actual neural networks is not established or empirically verified
Stochastic gradient case entirely unaddressed theoretically despite being standard in practice; unclear whether gradient noise naturally prevents convergence to hallucinated minimizers
Theorem 3.2 requires initialization close to hallucinated minimizers, but experiments show convergence from random initialization; basin of attraction is not characterized

Limited experimental scope: full-batch experiments only on MNIST with 2-layer networks; single realistic experiment (ResNet-18/CIFAR-100); missing ImageNet, diverse architectures, and ablation studies

Switching strategy appears ad-hoc: 10% threshold not derived from theory; Figure 5 shows improvements even at ρ=1.0 where SAM already works; improvements modest in realistic regimes (Figure 6: 77.05%→77.49%)
Unclear practical severity: hallucinated minimizers most problematic at large ρ and with full-batch gradients, but Figure 6 suggests typical practitioners use ρ∈[0.1,0.3] where methods are similar
Restrictive assumptions in Theorem 3.2 on eigenvalues of Sym(∇u(x_h)) are not empirically verified; unclear what fraction of hallucinated minimizers satisfy these conditions
SAM variants (ASAM, GSAM, FSAM) not analyzed; unclear if results generalize beyond vanilla SAM with normalized perturbation
No comparison to alternative potential solutions (adaptive ρ, gradient clipping, line search) or ablation on the switching fraction
